identity_admission.proof: At authoritative journal sequence 3186, only normalized SourceRecord versions are admitted to the ledger; a rejected record is refused and leaves no outbox row. Job identity is the content digest of the normalized version, and a contradicting payload under the same identity aborts the whole admission transaction.

pre_deploy.terminal_readback: A full controller tick drove a normalized SourceRecord through the real registry service. The registered entry was read back over HTTP at artifact_state draft, and metadata.distillation retained source_id, source_digest, and source_event_version across the round trip.

proof: Job identity is the SHA-256 content digest of the normalized source version, so admitting the same content twice returns one job and one committed version row.

Run-local correlation fields (ingest_run_id, source_ingest_run_id, trace_id) are excluded from the digest, so an identical re-crawl in a later run resolves to the committed version instead of creating a second job or failing admission.
Revised content produces a distinct digest, a distinct job, and a distinct versioned Registry draft; two revisions of one source yielded exactly two Registry entries.

A versioned job always derives its evidence item, bundle, and seed lineage from its admission-time digest, so a Registry outage followed by an intervening revision replays to the original seed identity.

Registry payload construction never resolves mutable production-note files by source id; a valid same-id note with conflicting title and hypothesis cannot replace the committed source, seed, evidence bundle/item, or checksum.
Repeated controller ticks after terminal success perform no further Registry write and leave one job and one seed.
A Registry write failure raises DistillationControllerError at stage registry_sync; the controller records a failure tick and no success, and consecutive_failures increments.
The failed job is parked as retry_wait with a backoff next_attempt_at and the failure reason, rather than being acknowledged.
After the attempt budget is exhausted the job becomes dead_letter and a durable dead-letter row retains the committed payload, so it stays redrivable.
A real connection failure against a port with nothing listening produces the same truthful degraded outcome as the simulated outage.
A job is acknowledged only after a terminal Registry readback; the write response alone never completes the job.

The source snapshot is committed in the same transaction as the outbox event, and versioned jobs always reload that snapshot, so a caller map containing a later revision cannot substitute the event's payload.
Materialization identity is digest-keyed at admission and does not depend on the later source version count.
Before conversion, the Registry sink fail-closed validates the job digest and version key plus exact seed, bundle, item, and source identity as one coherent request lineage.
metadata.distillation carries source_id, source_digest, source_event_version, and distillation_job_id into the Registry entry, preserving source-to-draft lineage.
The Registry sink receives the exact evidence item and bundle the seed was materialized from, keeping the registered artifact inside the StrategySpecSeed lineage.

A worker that claims a job and dies before reaching the Registry leaves an expired lease; the lease is recovered to pending and a later tick replays it to exactly one terminal draft with exactly one Registry write.
A Registry write that lands while its acknowledgement is lost is replayed by versioned readback: the second pass reaches done with no second Registry entry, one job, and one seed.
A completion presented with a stale lease token is rejected, so a resurrected worker cannot overwrite the outcome of the worker that superseded it.

A completion or terminal failure presented after lease_expires_at is rejected even before another worker reclaims the job; done, failed, skipped, and dead-letter transitions all fail closed at expiry.
A Registry outage followed by an intervening source revision replays the original job with the same evidence bundle and seed identity, while the revision receives a distinct identity.

A write-ack-loss replay after mutable same-id note mutation and a crossed timestamp boundary preserves the original seed created_at, rebuilds the identical payload and checksum, returns already_terminal, reaches done, and creates no dead letter.
Recovery is exercised through the real lease ledger and real spawned OS processes, and the replay outcome is asserted from the persisted ledger rather than from an in-test substitute.
Admission is a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: a contradicting payload under an existing version identity rolls back, leaving the committed version and outbox unchanged.
Exhausted delivery compensates into a durable dead-letter table that retains the committed payload and supports operator redispatch, which clears the dead letter with redrive attribution.

Registry artifacts in approved or retired state are never mutated; StrategySpec creation is atomic create-if-absent, and the job is marked skipped even when approval lands after the controller probe but before its POST.
This slice grants no broker, deployment, runtime-control, or live-capital mutation authority.
